name: Carnosine
short: Small trials are mixed: one 3-month trial reported more adverse events with carnosine (30%) than placebo (14%); two others found no difference in side effects or no serious side-effects.
text: In the cited sources, safety evidence for carnosine comes from randomised trials of 40 to 75 people in which it was added to existing treatment, and the results are mixed. In a 3-month trial in 75 adults with chronic schizophrenia, the carnosine group reported more adverse events (30%) than the placebo group (14%), while laboratory indices remained within acceptable ranges; the abstract does not describe the events or say whether the difference was statistically significant. In a 6-week trial in 58 patients with major depressive disorder taking citalopram, the frequency of side effects did not differ significantly between carnosine and placebo, and in a 12-week trial in 40 patients with diabetic nephropathy both groups tolerated treatment well with no serious side-effects and kidney function measures unchanged. No interaction data were found in the cited sources, although one of these trials gave carnosine alongside citalopram and another gave it as adjunctive treatment in schizophrenia.
